claims.text: OpenAI RSS timestamped the Images 2.5 announcement at 2026-09-08T11:30:00Z.
OpenAI says Images 2.5 generation latency is up to 50 per cent lower than Images 2.0.
OpenAI says Images 2.5 better preserves subjects, composition and details through selective and repeated edits.
ChatGPT adds Sketch, templates, comments on images and optional prompt sharing.
OpenAI says Images 2.5 is rolling out across ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work and Codex on desktop, mobile and web.
OpenAI positions Flare for fast everyday image generation and Sunburst for workflows where editing precision matters.
claims.sourceLocator: Launch page lines 99-101; model summaries; guide lines 827-829

claims.text: Both API models accept text and image inputs, produce image outputs and support low, medium, high, xhigh, max and auto quality settings.
claims.sourceLocator: Both model summaries lines 817-838 and modalities

claims.text: Both models expose dated 2026-09-08 snapshot identifiers.
The Image API handles generation or edits from a prompt, while the Responses API adds conversational and multi-step editing.
OpenAI lists equal token rates for Flare and Sunburst but warns that equal rates do not mean equal cost per image because consumption varies by model and quality.
The launch page does not publish an independent Images 2.5 benchmark for selective or multi-round editing.
claims.sourceLocator: Full launch-page inspection; examples and customer statements are company-selected

claims.text: I2EBench2.0 separates single-round and multi-round evaluation and uses 16 single-round and seven multi-round dimensions.
I2EBench2.0 predates and does not evaluate Images 2.5.
claims.sourceLocator: Paper submission 14 June 2026 versus release 8 September 2026

claims.text: A useful adoption trial should score both the requested change and declared invariants after every edit.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us recommendation from vendor preservation claims and independent evaluation dimensions

claims.text: Cost and time per accepted asset are more decision-relevant than first-response latency alone.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us recommendation from latency, token-consumption and multi-round evaluation evidence

claims.text: The system card says greater realism could enable more convincing deepfakes without safeguards.
OpenAI describes upstream checks, input monitoring and output blocking in the safety stack.
On OpenAI's fixed adversarial set, unsafe images presented were 1.09 per cent for Sunburst, 1.41 per cent for Flare and 1.64 per cent for Images 2.0.
No unsafe-presented difference met OpenAI's significance threshold; automated labels may be wrong and sample sizes affect precision.
The system-card figures establish a bounded vendor test, not uniform safety across workflows.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us interpretation of evaluation design and stated limitations

claims.text: OpenAI says Images 2.5 uses C2PA metadata and SynthID invisible watermarking across ChatGPT, Codex and the API.
NIST says provenance does not guarantee trust, no technique is comprehensive alone and robustness must cover ordinary transformations and tampering.
Teams should inspect provenance at each real delivery transformation instead of assuming generator-level marking survives.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us recommendation from the system card and NIST robustness boundaries

claims.text: Images 2.5 earns a controlled workflow trial but not an automatic switch.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us conclusion from shipped availability, evidence limits and measurable adoption criteria
